content.comment_body: Hello, I would like to connect two [product_name] [article_no] devices using Ethernet in order to exchange digital information between them. For example, I need to detect on one device whether a digital input on the other device is active. Can anyone help with the Ethernet connection settings—perhaps with an example or tutorial? I was unable to find any on this forum. Thank you for any replies, [user_name].

On this page of [company_name], you can find examples showing communication between [article_no] devices, including both master/master and master/slave configurations. Personally, I recommend the master/master setup. With master/master, each module runs its own program, whereas with master/slave, only the master module has a program and the slave acts as an extension module. [url]

Thank you [user_name], everything is working now! I'm noticing a transmission delay between the devices—the input state sent from one master to the other is delayed by 30 to 250 ms. Is it possible to minimize this delay? Could master/slave communication offer shorter latency? Regards.
Sorry, I don't have an answer to that.
I've checked, and the communication delay in master/slave mode is similar.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are setting up Ethernet communication between two [product_name] [article_no] modules to exchange digital signals. Documentation and shared examples enabled a successful connection, but a consistent delay (30–250 ms) occurs in both master/master and master/slave modes. The community wants to reduce this latency, though no clear built-in solution has been identified.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate real-time or near real-time communication with minimal delay when digital inputs are exchanged between the two [product_name] [article_no] devices.
